cros-kernel2: No need to hardcode '-m elf_x86_64' The kernel ebuild was hardcoding '-m elf_x86_64' into the "LD" variable, which was rather ugly. Presumably this was needed due to the fact that we were improperly passing LDFLAGS into the kernel because the kernel sets LDFLAGS to '-m elf_$(UTS_MACHINE)'. That's now fixed as of commit c1440c3ce817 ("cros-kernel2: Pass most stuff to kernel make as env vars, not cmdline args"). Since we have the fix let's remove the ugliness. Tested by printing the value of LD and LDFLAGS using $(info): Before c1440c3ce817: USE=x32 emerge ... => "-m elf_x86_64" in "LD" emerge ... => no "-m elf_x86_64" anywhere After c1440c3ce817: USE=x32 emerge ... => "-m elf_x86_64" in _both_ "LD" and "LDFLAGS" emerge ... => "-m elf_x86_64" in "LDFLAGS" BUG=None TEST=See above Change-Id: I07d5c19e6410975f1dbccccd9f96f774f4de16be Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/696183 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

cros-kernel2: Unset CFLAGS In general the kernel doesn't expect CFLAGS to be set. As described in the text of this change: The kernel doesn't use CFLAGS and doesn't expect it to be passed in. Let's be explicit that it won't do anything by unsetting CFLAGS. In general the kernel manages its own tools flags and doesn't expect someone external to pass flags in unless those flags have been very specifically tailored to interact well with the kernel Makefiles. In that case we pass in flags with KCFLAGS which is documented to be not a full set of flags but as "additional" flags. In general the kernel Makefiles carefully adjust their flags in various sub-directories to get the needed result. The kernel has CONFIG_ options for adjusting compiler flags and self-adjusts itself depending on whether it detects clang or not. NOTE: Right now, due to what's probably a bug, having CFLAGS set when you compile the kernel actually _does_ affect something. If you have the right set of options then the kernel's Makefile will build stuff from the tools/ Makefile. In that particular case the kernel actually uses CFLAGS for building host tools. We should probably fix that in the kernel itself so that when it calls into tools/ it passes HOSTCFLAGS (which the main kernel Makefile uses) in as CFLAGS (which the tools Makefiles use). BUG=chromium:767565 TEST=Compile a bunch of kernels Change-Id: If695dbd0b3eb9015bf4806de8818c7512e649026 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/696185 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

Reorganize the ignore_failures vs. !ignore_failures logic a bit, and add a new TestFail() condition for when we get no results and haven't asked for 'ignore_failures=True'. BUG=chromium:629137 TEST=network_AttenuatedPerf, with high attenuation (causing association failures on certain boards) Change-Id: I7881391eed3bb10a8b58573e1567a6c3e5aaea0b Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/696267 Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org>

netperf: limit extent of retries, timeout delays When run with 'ignore_failures' (e.g., with AttenuatedPerf), we forgive all failure and just wait until the end to collect a None result. This is pointless and time-wasting, especially on attenuated tests, where we ramp up attenuation until the client gets abysmal performance (and likely disconnects from the AP eventually). We should not keep trying to get 10 samples (MEASUREMENT_MAX_SAMPLES) when we see multiple None results (i.e., errors). Limit this to 2 failures, and abort on the 3rd. Also, CL:217970 increased the netperf timeout from a 10 second margin (on top of test time) to 120 seconds, with no explanation. This seems excessively high for a 10-second test. And note that we do hit this timeout sometimes, when running AttenuatedPerf. So let's decrease that to 60 seconds, which should still be conservative, but should save us several times that much on some tests, since netperf sessions often include multiple retries. BUG=none TEST=network_WiFi_AttenuatedPerf Change-Id: I7712fbcb39176c28b037231bb6c4708579672ec4 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/696671 Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org>

cave: audio-config: Decrease lower end speaker volume There have been many people complaining that cave doesn't have volume settings low enough for listening in a quiet environment. I noticed this as well because cave is my regular device. Set the volume levels for the last part of the speaker volume curve so they drop off much faster and volume four, the lowest reachable from the buttons, is low enough when in a quiet room. network_WiFi_AttenuatedPerf: autodetect/report max attenuation CL:286195 changed both the min and max attenuation values we would use. This artificially restricted us to a range of +20 dB, which doesn't really cover as much range as we'd like, in some cases. Let's try to bump that back up. However, in testing more extreme attenuation, I've found that at least on some DUTs, we can't even connect to the AP. Our netperf code isn't able to promptly handle this condition, as the current logic tries for 10 samples (or failures), each consisting of up to 3 retries, and a 2 minute timeout. That means it will take 1 hour for a run to complete in the null case where we haven't even associated correctly. We should probably improve the netperf logic to handle this a little better too, but as a first step, we can check for a connection before kicking off a session. So this CL: (a) adds a basic connectivity test for each attenuation level (b) stops testing an attenuation level if any netperf session returns no result (c) logs (and reports to the keyval storage) the maximum attenuation reached (d) expands the theoretical max attenuation to 100dB, instead of "start + 20" Example runs now look something like this: INFO | autoserv| RvR test: current attenuation = 79 dB INFO | autoserv| Waiting for AttenuatedPerf_a_4fgeb_ch1 to reach one of ['ready', 'portal', 'online']... INFO | autoserv| ...ended up in state 'online' (success) after 0.007059 seconds. INFO | autoserv| Pinging from the client. INFO | autoserv| Could not establish connection at 79 dB INFO | autoserv| Error: Ping command failed with code=1 INFO | autoserv| Running time 968.1 seconds. INFO | autoserv| Reached attenuation of: 75 dB (signal -76 dBm) BUG=none TEST=network_WiFi_AttenuatedPerf, see expanded atten values tested Change-Id: Ie435ecc80ac78017dc9f003dd2cf0c4ef446323b Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/695707 Reviewed-by: Harpreet Grewal <harpreet@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org>
